author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.
imageAlt: Sovereign commerce infrastructure for digital creators blocked by Stripe and PayPal in Nigeria
imageCaption: Sovereign infrastructure routes around Stripe and PayPal restrictions permanently — not a workaround, a different architecture.

content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional payment infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-explained-digital-2|cloudflare]] Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/google-apps-script-digital-commerce-automation-what-actually-4|COREMERCH guide to google]]-apps-script-digital-commerce-automation-explained-digital-3|Google Apps]] Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Digital products

This is not about workarounds or hacks. It's about building a base-layer infrastructure that allows creators to take control of their digital commerce ecosystems. With sovereign commerce infrastructure, you don't rent a platform; you own the architecture. This means no reliance on Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, or other platforms that can suspend or restrict your account at any time. By deploying your own infrastructure, you can sell digital products without the fear of platform restrictions or account suspensions.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

Sovereign commerce infrastructure relies on a combination of free and paid tools that provide a complete digital commerce stack. This includes GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. By integrating these tools, you can create a seamless digital commerce experience for your customers while maintaining full control over your infrastructure.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This solution is designed for digital creators in countries where Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle are unavailable or severely restricted. This includes Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Cameroon, Tanzania, the Philippines, and other regions where digital commerce growth is stifled by platform restrictions. By providing a permanent structural alternative, we empower creators to take control of their digital commerce ecosystems and reach their full potential.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure empowers digital creators to take control of their ecosystems.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The key components of sovereign commerce infrastructure include GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. These components work together to provide a seamless digital commerce experience for customers while maintaining full control over the infrastructure.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

The storefront in a COREMERCH deployment is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. It costs nothing to host. It scales to any traffic level automatically. It cannot be taken down by a payment platform's compliance decision because the hosting and the payment layer are completely separate infrastructure. Your buyer experience is clean and professional — a product page, a crypto checkout with QR code generation and live price feeds, and an automatic delivery email within 30 seconds of payment. Every component runs under your own accounts. If COREMERCH closed tomorrow, every store deployed would continue running exactly as it does today. That is what infrastructure ownership means.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

The direct answer is NOWPayments combined with a sovereign commerce stack. NOWPayments is a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 coins, charges 0.5% per transaction, and sends a webhook to your backend the moment payment confirms on-chain. Your backend — a Cloudflare Worker in Stack 02, a Google Apps Script Web App in Stack 01 — receives the webhook, verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email automatically. There is no platform that can suspend your access, no compliance team that can flag your account, no payout schedule that delays your revenue, and no company that can change the rules on you tomorrow.
Selling digital products without platform restrictions requires a fundamental shift in architecture.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your own sovereign commerce infrastructure, follow these steps: deploy your website using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, integrate Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, set up Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, configure Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, and integrate NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. Don't forget to load 5 products, configure SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and test your infrastructure before handoff.
